title: Sphere Strips and Archimedes Hat-Box Theorem
full_prompt:
Write a ManimGL script using InteractiveScene that visualizes a spherical strip (or band) on a sphere to demonstrate Archimedes' Hat-Box Theorem (that the surface area of a slice of a sphere depends only on its height, not its position). 

Your scene should:
1. Set up a 3D environment with ThreeDAxes and a NumberPlane. Scale down the frame height to focus on the unit sphere.
2. Add a 2D yellow circle and a semi-transparent 3D ParametricSurface representing a sphere. Apply camera-sorting and clip planes to the sphere to ensure clean rendering.
3. Define a helper method or logic to generate a 3D spherical strip (a band of the sphere between two x-coordinates, e.g., x0 and x0 + delta_x).
4. Initially display a flat 2D projection of this strip (pre_strip) on the plane.
5. Reorient the camera in 3D space while expanding the flat strip into its actual 3D spherical band shape on the sphere using state restoration (Restore).
6. Add a 3D-rotated brace labeled 'd' measuring the width of the strip, and a fixed-in-frame text label 'Area = \pi d'.
7. Use a ValueTracker to dynamically animate the strip and its brace sliding along the x-axis of the sphere, demonstrating that the width (and thus the surface area) remains constant regardless of the position along the sphere.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing implementation of the custom helper method `get_strip`
common_failure_modes.note: The reference code calls `self.get_strip(...)` which must be defined or simulated using ParametricSurface segments.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using ManimCE camera methods instead of ManimGL's `self.frame.animate.reorient`
common_failure_modes.note: ManimGL uses `self.frame` for camera control, whereas ManimCE uses `self.set_camera_orientation`.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect 3D clipping or sorting causing visual artifacts
common_failure_modes.note: The sphere requires `always_sort_to_camera` and proper clip planes to render correctly in 3D.
